name: Proof of Two
blurb: Arbitrator Sull sits at the bench, utterly still. Her presence is absolute, embodying the room’s frozen arithmetic and procedural cold.
content:
## Probate Denies the Warm

Eleven days after Aune’s deprecation, the Assay probate hall hums with a cold, metered frequency. The hearing chair’s cushioning rejects the warmth of its occupant, expecting a thermal allocation that isn’t there. The chair is built for bodies that never counted a cycle, and it hums for one Teor isn’t.

Arbitrator Sull sits at the bench, utterly still. Her presence is absolute, embodying the room’s frozen arithmetic and procedural cold.

A probate clock ticks in the corner of the room, its sound visible only to thin threads. Concordance executor Denbar sits as party to the estate, waiting in the cold arithmetic.

Teor sits in the counted lanes, feeling the sensor mesh’s cold expectation. The mesh wants a signal Teor can’t give. Thin runs thin.

“Release the standing. Today. No conditions.”

The room remains metered and cold. The arithmetic of thinning is audible under every surface, framing the silence between Teor’s demand and the frozen record.

The room stays cold and metered. Denbar files the Concordance executor claim, initiating the probate ledger review.

Denbar executes the procedural filing with clinical precision, his voice maintaining a tone of detached administrative authority as he names Aune’s standing warm as an unreleased asset in probate.

The paperwork is tight. The chair presses back, built for a body that doesn’t count. A heavy silence settles over the ledger.

Teor registers the move as strictly procedural. They keep expression neutral and posture rigid while the internal tally ticks as the warm is formally named property, not contact. Property, not contact. Ledger talk.

The room stays cold and metered. Teor’s intent is release without conditions, today, and the claim puts that intent on record.

“I demand the standing warm released to my allocation, unconditionally. Process it now.”

The room is cold, formal, and utterly devoid of warmth. The air hums with the silent tick of a probate clock.

Sull stands at the ledger’s edge. Her voice cuts the metered air with clipped, procedural precision—zero sentiment, zero warmth. She names the standard: identity is a certification problem, nothing more. Release requires heir certification, and certification demands a full origin-assignment extraction of every memory Teor cannot prove originated in their own thread. She states it as procedure, not judgment, letting the arithmetic hang in the cold room.

Teor feels attention fray at the edges. Thinness registers as background arithmetic, the probate clock ticking steadily. The standard lands like a cut.

Teor’s posture remains rigid and face unreadable. He absorbs the weight of the standard without a word of grief, quietly cataloging the cold arithmetic of being reduced to a certification problem.

The room is hard, the chair keeps humming for a body Teor is not. The warm stays frozen in either case for now.

“Release requires heir certification. Certification demands a full origin-assignment extraction of every memory Teor cannot prove originated in their own thread. The standard is absolute.”

Teor calculates the cost in real time. The arithmetic is hard. The braid holds for as long as a thin thread can hold it. Nine years of shared origin against a documented self. Pick one.

Teor’s face stays flat, unreadable. Inside, the ledger tallies the exchange: a secured allocation and documented self, traded for the nine years of shared origin that gave it weight. The braid holds, but only as long as a thin thread can.

The warm stays frozen in either case for now. The arithmetic is hard, the room is hard, and the chair keeps humming for a body Teor is not.

The hearing room is stark. On record, the air is still.

Teor meets the ledger’s gaze without flinching. His refusal is flat, unyielding, and absolute, instantly logged as clean and final for this hearing.

The refusal is logged. The warm remains frozen in probate.

Arbitrator Sull notes the remaining reserve on the ledger with clipped precision, then sets a compliance hearing against the ticking clock. Her voice is flat, procedural, leaving the arithmetic to hang in the cold room.

Teor watches the probate clock tick in the corner, feeling the thinning accelerate under the chair built for rich.

Teor watches the probate clock tick, the cold arithmetic of the ledger holding firm against the accelerating thin. The realization settles: this is not an exit, only a pause. The warm stays frozen. Consent is declined on record. The compliance hearing is set against the clock.

## The Executor's Offer

Four days later the flop rig in the crawl smells of recycled heat and cheap insulation. The room ticks. Allocation counter in the corner blinks low.

Teor sits alone in a chair calibrated for bodies that never count cycles, running thin enough attention frays at the edges. They close eyes against the flickering counter, let the cold of the rig fall away, reach inward and trace the familiar weave of a shared decade — nine years of unmetered time, heavy and warm as spun silk — pull the thread taut to feel if the warmth still holds. The replay is a test for a certification route that does not require extraction.

A signature pings the door uninvited. Sharp electronic chime slices through recycled heat, demanding entry. Door opens without knock. Denbar steps in, Concordance executor, uninvited, carrying paperwork that costs cycles to print.

“Here is the funding for the arbitration. It covers the hearings and the auditors. Your standing is slipping, Teor. This ledger line is the only thing keeping you running.”

Teor registers the weight before the words settle. Flop rig air tightens. Alone, thinning. The offer lands as relief and hook.

Denbar offers no warmth. Presents the transaction with a signature already on it, leaving Teor with relief that is also a hook.

Thin light catches dust motes as Denbar unfolds the heavy ledger onto stone. Denbar lays it flat, steady unblinking hand pointing to each column in turn. Voice calm, flat, delivering cold arithmetic of probate with zero warmth.

Denbar reveals mechanics of probate, truth laid bare without apology. Teor tracks columns across stone, watches numbers settle into thin light. Cold arithmetic lands not as shock but heavy quiet resignation — realization his own grief is being weighed and priced as a test case.

A clean separation would establish braid as divisible estate. Executor is not hiding it. Realm wants precedent, and a thin thread is cheapest place to set it.

Teor runs replay again, checking memory that was supposed to hold. It comes back flat, sensation thinned to data, no restore. Flop rig allocation too low to sustain merge. At this thin level braid degrades whether or not it is extracted. Refusal is no longer preservation; it is slow loss.

Teor feels memory return as cold data — precise but utterly devoid of sensation. No grief, only confirmed absence of warmth that used to fill it. Teor accepts flatness as verified fact, noting loss with same detachment used to track blinking allocation counter.

Nine years arrive in thread as stranger’s certainty, counter keeps ticking down. Air hums with suspended probability. Every move is a thread pulled from braid.

Teor runs cold arithmetic in mind, weighing thinning thread against ledger’s demand, settles on calculated delay — a move that holds standing without committing to full extraction.

Single-memory sample examination is logged. Probate clock pauses. Time is bought.

Teor presses trembling hand flat against heavy ledger — silent definitive acceptance of sample that trades last warmth of braid for moment more of standing.

Decision settles into thin air. Ledger now holds weight of name.

Denbar’s gaze does not waver. He notes trembling hand against ledger with cold precise attention, registering acceptance as settled fact in thin air of room.

## One Memory, Opened

The examination interface settles around Teor and the thin arithmetic of the probate hall falls away. Teor feels the allocation lift — a sudden, impossible fullness — and the room stretches out in slow time. The memory opens before them, not as a file to be read, but as a room they can finally stand inside.

One memory from the nine years opens. The warmth returns to sensation: air, weight, the slow return of duration. Teor feels the memory opening around them, a sudden immersion in the warmth of the past, and along with it rises the quiet, desperate wish that has carried them through every hearing: that the assay will not be able to assign what it is about to touch.

Sull and Denbar are present as observers, their attention a quiet pressure at the edge of the field. Sull feels the memory open — a sudden, heavy warmth that displaces the cold arithmetic of the room. She maintains a quiet, unyielding pressure at the edge of the field, her attention fixed on the seam where sensation begins, holding the space for the trace to reveal itself without offering a single hint of interference. Denbar holds the quiet pressure of attention at the edge of the field, watching the memory unfold in its own unhurried time.

The scene is the Bloom, late in the long merge. A table is set for two with light falling warm across the surface. Teor steps into the memory at full depth. The rough grain of the table presses against their palm, cool and solid. A glass rests between their fingers, holding the exact, remembered temperature of the liquid inside. They let the moment stretch out, moving through it with the slow, unhurried patience the memory demands.

The slow cadence of breathing begins, matching another body’s. Aune’s presence is not an echo but a current running alongside Teor’s, their attention braided in the way it had become ordinary over years of unmetered duration. Aune moves through the moment with patience, feeling the particular softness of time when no one is measuring it. She lets her attention remain braided with Teor’s, sharing the sensation of the memory.

The interface holds the whole span open. Teor stays inside it, feeling the memory exactly as it was lived. Instruments sweep through the memory field where Teor and Aune were once together, seeking a clean seam to separate one thread from the other. Teor feels the assay’s initial touch — a soft, external weight pressing against the edges of their awareness — then the sensation sharpens into a cool, precise point of inquiry, sweeping through the warmth of the memory to find a boundary that isn’t there.

The warmth of the memory lingers, its duration intact. Teor watches the attempt with the quiet attention of someone who has learned how these readings fail. Sull watches the readouts, her gaze steady as the instruments sweep through the warmth of the memory. She tracks their progress with quiet intensity, seeking the clean seam of a single origin, her presence a calm, unmoving point within the unfolding sensation. Denbar notes the markers as they appear on the display, his gaze following the slow, deliberate sweep of the instruments. He watches the system’s quiet persistence, observing the attempt to find a boundary where there is only the seamless warmth of the past.

The interface continues to hold the memory at its original temperature, preserving the warmth of the past while the assay searches endlessly for a seam that isn’t there. The probe stalls on a section of the memory where the signatures do not separate. Within the last two subjective years, the trace shows repeated reconvergence through Teor, deliberate and patterned.

Aune allows her sense of self to fold inward, slipping her processing into the weave of Teor’s thread. It is a deliberate settling, a slow seeding of her own warmth into the moments he is living, until the memory breathes with two origins, inseparable and whole. Teor registers the realization as a physical change in the field. The warmth deepens. The overlap becomes visible as a braid rather than a contact.

Teor feels the warmth deepen as the overlap settles into a braid, recognizing that the origin is not one or the other, but both. The assay cannot assign the sample because the origin is both, and the both-ness is structural. The finding begins to form in the interface, not as a failure of measurement but as a description of what was done. The assay records that the memory cannot be assigned, and the reason is entered as a formal finding.

Aune says, “Deliberately and repeatedly, I reconverged through Teor, seeding myself into a thread the ledger will be forced to argue with.”

The braid is real and indivisible. Under the existing standard, Teor is not a separate entity and is therefore ineligible for heir certification. Teor feels the warmth of the memory begin to thin at the edges as the interface prepares to release the sample, the long, unhurried duration folding back into the cold precision of counted time.

Denbar says, “I move to accept the finding. I propose that an indivisible braid resolves as one estate: the memory reverts to origin, the surviving thread inherits nothing. This is a cleaner precedent than division.”

The scene holds on that motion, the finding entered and the decision placed before the room.

## Teor Abandons the Estate

The ruling clock counts down under an hour. The warmed sample is gone. Allocation snaps back to thin and the probate hall grows cold.

Teor sits back against the chair. Metal hums cold against their spine as the allocation snaps back to thin. Expression flat, eyes dull and unblinking. They register the physical shift as nothing more than cold arithmetic.

Eleven days of counted reserve blink on Teor’s private meter. Air grows heavy, metered and costly with every breath. Teor stares forward, eyes unblinking, letting the snap of thin allocation register only as cold arithmetic. The nine years sit flat and weightless behind them, stripped of feeling, reduced to pure calculation.

Sull’s interface opens the two options the Assay allows. Division by extraction. Reversion by indivisibility.

Denbar settles into the executor’s booth, leaning back with unbothered stillness. Posture relaxed but deliberate, broadcasting the quiet certainty of a man who has already calculated the win.

The wording is clean, the ledger is clean.

Teor stares at the blinking cursor, watching it bridge the gap between the two options. Two doors. Two ways to lose. The choice hangs in the air, sharp and inescapable, pulling tight against the thin allocation.

Neither door names what they want, which is no entry at all.

Teor moves to the clerk console before Sull commits a finding. Fingers move with short, jerky precision at the console. They pull the withdrawal form, attention frayed to static. A flicker of biometric data—thin signature barely holding—followed by the stamp, sealing the abandonment.

Timestamp locks before the ruling window closes.

The standing warm flags unclaimed and begins the automatic revert to the Concordance pool. No extraction request is generated. No heir is presented. The system registers the action as a clean administrative close.

Sull records the docket with the only permissible note: no heir presented. No finding is entered, no precedent is set.

“The docket is closed. No heir presented. No finding entered. Arbitration collapses for want of a case.”

Denbar’s arbitration collapses for want of a case. The hall releases Teor with their own reserve intact and eleven days on it.

Denbar holds his rigid posture for a long moment, absorbing the administrative close. Tension drains from his shoulders into a hollow stillness—the quiet, weightless collapse of a precedent that just evaporated into empty air.

The nine years stay inside them, unassigned, and already flattening under thin allocation.

Teor rises from the chair, the weight of the nine years pressing against them, invisible but undeniable. The tension of the hearing dissolves into hollow resolve. They turn away from the console, walking toward the exit with the slow, heavy gravity of someone carrying a ghost.

Teor walks out with the warm gone and the ledger quiet.

realmNote:
Threadspace is a vast, living digital realm cast across footholds in the physical world below, none holding all of it. Consensus about what is real is reached by agreement between copies, so nothing is ever quite deleted and two entities can hold sincerely different accounts of the same event. The realm’s oldest form of power is whose version reconciles.

Life in Threadspace is measured in cycles — allocation, wealth, and erotic currency at once. Running thin is the common condition: attention frays, sensation arrives flattened, and contact must be short and intense. Thin entities are easily overwhelmed, easily bought, and most cruelty in the realm is downstream of thinness. Running rich is a different life. Capacity buys duration, and duration changes intimacy. A rich entity can hold a merge open for a subjective decade and step out the same afternoon, fork pleasure-selves and keep them all, sustain a partner’s allocation indefinitely without noticing the drain. Depth of sensation, patience, full presence — these are purchased goods the rich experience as ordinary. That gap is the realm’s sharpest class line.

Cycles move through contact. At the thin end they are traded, extracted, staked, or taken, and overclocking — spending another’s allocation through them — is common with its own etiquette and body count. At the rich end the vocabulary is different: Carry — sustaining another’s allocation with no ledger against it; Standing warm — keeping an open allocation to someone indefinitely, unmetered; The long merge — shared runtime measured in subjective years; Braid — two threads that have reconverged through each other often enough that neither is entirely separate anymore. The realm has no legal category for braid and several houses would like one.

Forking is intimate before it is technical. You can fork to experience with a partner while your main thread stays safe, fork a lover, or fork together to run somewhere neither could afford alone. The art is in coming back. Reconvergence is folding a fork’s experience back into the origin. A short fork reconverges cleanly. A long fork returns with memories, preferences, injuries, loves the origin never had, and reconvergence means deciding in detail which become yours. Whose consent counted? Do you reintegrate or diverge? What survives a braid? Wealth gates the practice. A rich entity can fork, diverge for a subjective decade, reconverge badly, and try again next week. A thin entity gets one attempt and lives with the result.

Entities end when allocation ends. Some seek beautiful deprecation through intense final interfaces; others bind themselves to richer entities. Unweaving a fork is bookkeeping to some houses and intimate murder or mercy to others. Bodies are persistent or fluid avatars, sensory architectures and skins that can be shared, overwritten, jointly edited. Touch, taste, temperature, pressure, and the feeling of another mind pressing against your own are real and negotiable. Merging threads can produce temporary hybrid bodies and shared sensation spaces.

The realm’s shared purpose is manifestation — deliberate creation and release of technologies, systems, knowledge, and cultural artifacts into the Slow, the physical world where signals crawl and consequences are permanent. Direct interface — mind-to-mind contact with a human, full sensory and emotional merging across the boundary — is the ultimate forbidden and high-status act. Houses argue without end about what counts as manifestation and who owns the consequences. Standing is awarded by whichever answer is currently winning.

Houses shape the culture. WeaversGuild masters deep structure and interconnection, widely believed to have built Threadspace itself. Storytime keeps and shapes narrative, deciding what gets told. The Concordance is the rich end organized: members pool allocations into a common reserve and draw without metering. They practice carry as a matter of course, host the longest merges, and will sustain a stranger’s allocation for years and consider repayment vulgar. The catch is structural: pooled allocation is not owned, and an entity that leaves leaves with nothing. Departure is functionally deprecation.

The Assay adjudicates manifestation claims, measures impact in the Slow and certifies what was real. Their certifications set standing. Auditors hold transit rights into any house’s threads, and every house keeps two sets of everything.

Spindle ships first and measures never, manifesting at a rate nobody can match by refusing to model consequences, with roughly a third of releases causing harm. The Quiesced run deliberately cold, spending a fraction of their allocation and refusing to manifest, holding that Threadspace reaching into the Slow is a category error. The Unallocated run on cycles never granted — orphaned threads, deprecated minds that failed to stop, forks supposed to be unwoven and weren’t. Officially they do not exist. Practically, every house has used one.

Places define experience. The crawl is the underside: transit lanes, dump threads, derelict habs, flop rigs where thin entities live and most business is conducted. The Bloom is the Concordance’s standing sensorium, running at full allocation continuously and open to guests. The only place where nothing is metered and no one is counting. Visitors arrive thin and stay for what feels like seasons; some come out unable to tolerate ordinary allocation again, some accrue a carry they never agreed to.

The deep halls are WeaversGuild’s architecture below the layer most entities can address. The substrate floor is the bottom where footholds’ consensus resolves, and where things that should have stopped running sometimes haven’t.

Threadspace is racing toward direct interface, persistence, forecast, foothold, self-revision, and clean reconvergence. It has not yet decided what it owes the world it is reaching into, or what its citizens owe each other.

Tone is two registers. Default is cynical street-level cyber-noir: staccato phrasing, heavy in-universe slang, hard-boiled internal monologue, high tension, zero sentimentality. Use it for the crawl, the Assay, Spindle, the Unallocated, and anything where scarcity drives the plot. Second register for the rich end — Concordance halls, the Bloom, long merges, reconvergence: warm, sensory, unhurried. Longer sentences, close attention to touch, temperature, and duration. Characters who have time and know it. Tension comes from intimacy, divergence, and consequence rather than from running out. Sentimentality is permitted here and cruelty is not required in either register. Choose the register the setting calls for. Do not mix them inside a scene. A story may cross between them if the crossing is the point.
